   the 20.0227 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50%

findings.title: The pipette draws air from tube A2 in slot 2: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 55 the p20_single_gen2 draws 1 ul from polymerase (tube A2 in slot 2) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it once, after 11 times in the liquid; 1 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
findings.explanation: At line 56 the robot put polymerase into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3 (this line did it 11 times). Take well A1 in slot 3: at that moment it held 14 ul, only 10 ul of it water or buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 59, to make the 20.0227 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 12 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 46 the tip went into sample 1 (tube A6 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube B1 in slot 2), sample 3 (tube B2 in slot 2), sample 4 (tube B3 in slot 2) and 8 more while it still carried buffer (tube A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 46 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
